analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 03.11.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 51bps to 7541 (+10% ytd). SOX fell another 3% (still +45% ytd) and Non-Profitable Tech fell 5% (-19% ytd). VIX rose 9% to 21. Kospi was also trading down 4%.
Apple and Palantir both traded down 3% post market despite earnings, which were not enough for the market.
Marvell (written 'Marvel' in the note, -11%) proposed to acquire Lumentum (-17%) in an all-share deal.
US 10-year yield is 4.91%, Brent is lower at $105 on Iran and Ukraine hopes, Gold is $3921 and Bitcoin is $77k. US midterms are today, AMD reports post market, and NFP is on Friday.
Trump signalled progress toward a possible agreement with Iran ('it looks like that's coming together very nicely'), pushing oil lower.

Prediction markets imply over 90% odds that Democrats win the House and over 65% that they win the Senate. GS expects no major fiscal policy change over the next 2 years, but spending could increase. Fiscal deadlines (spending authority extension, debt limit increase) would be the main legislative focus.

Apple beat on EPS, revenue and gross margin. GS is positive on the iPhone refresh cycle (iPhone Duo, foldable) but flags near-term Services headwinds from the App Store, an uncertain China outlook, softer 3P licensing (TAC) that was worse than expected, and memory cost inflation as a multi-quarter overhang.
Google raised EUR 6bn in its second euro bond sale this year at higher yields than its May deal, with maturities of 2-19 years and over EUR 17bn of orders. The 2045 bond yields roughly 5.2% in euros.

With 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, 3Q26 EPS growth is on track for 33% yoy, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in decades outside post-recession recoveries. The pace of upward revisions has slowed. GS says 3Q results support its view that AI capex growth is peaking while spending keeps growing.

A suspected second wave of cyberattacks hit supermarket refrigerators across Europe, raising fridge temperatures and spoiling food at dozens of stores. Ahold and Colruyt confirmed the hacks. GS points to its 16-stock Cyber basket (GSTMTCYB Index).

GS estimates the AI financing need through FY28 at about $65bn to support about $180bn of capex (offset by about $35bn of prepayments and $80bn of operating cash flow). This compares with Oracle's roughly $20bn of capital needed, with $220bn of capex offset by about $110bn of vendor financing, BYOH and prepayments.

Hedge fund performance in October: Fundamental L/S -3.5% and Systematic L/S -3.6%, the first time since 2016 that both cohorts fell 3% or more in a month. Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling and net leverage fell at the fastest pace since March.

GS midterm trades under a Democratic sweep: long ACA Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA), AI Power (GSENEPOW) over ex-Power AI hardware (GSTMTAIH), and a corporate tax basket (GSPUTAXP) where 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated and the risk is a higher rate beyond 2029.
G10 consumers continue to benefit from healthy balance sheets and labor markets, but real income growth remains soft in most developed markets.
November typically delivers about 10.1% of yearly buyback spend (2nd strongest month after August). YTD repurchase authorizations are $1341bn (+14% yoy).
GS expects a second and final Fed hike in December, with a third hike in March possible if inflation comes in higher than expected.

The Nasdaq is down about 611bps over the last 3 sessions, the biggest 3-day slide since Liberation Day (about 20 months ago). The equal-weight S&P is up about 1% over the same stretch, and the Russell 2000 (+13% ytd) is now outperforming the Nasdaq (+11% ytd) in 2026.
24.6% of firms use AI in regular business functions (+0.8pp from September), and 28.6% expect to use AI in the next 6 months.
